_readme: Which Playwright specs a pull request to a branch other than main runs. Read by scripts/ci/select-e2e.mjs.
A pull request to main, a push to main or next-release, a release, the nightly run and a manual run of e2e-full.yml run the whole suite and ignore this file.
Otherwise the run is: the spec files the PR adds or changes, plus 'smoke', plus the specs of every rule whose paths match a changed file.

A changed file matching 'hubs', or one under static/ or app/ that matches no rule, also adds 'core'. It no longer runs the whole suite: the full run on the next push to next-release catches what core misses.
A changed file matching 'full' runs the whole suite: these change how the suite itself runs. So does a changed non-spec file under tests/e2e/ that matches no rule.

uv.lock and pyproject.toml are hubs, not full: a dependency change can move backend behaviour the core set exercises, but it does not change how Playwright runs, and the desktop-update-gate check covers the lock separately.

Why the core set is these specs: each drives a hub through the real UI. help-mode reaches every control and its i18n.js sentence; artist-languages switches the UI language; partial-stems and export-menu read stems through state.js, mixer.js and app/api/stems.py; karaoke crosses mode.js, mixer.js, transport.js, sections.js and /api/jobs; master-live builds the master bus; transpose and speed-control drive the audio engine's pitch and speed; footer-time checks transport.js against the engine clock; zoom redraws the multitrack vendor lanes; lane-alignment and track-header lay out the mixer rows over --lane-h; playback-memory runs chunkedAudioEngine.js; trash-restore moves library rows through catalog.js and app/api/jobs.py; job-form-submit and error-banner cover job.js and the composer form; boot-failure covers main.js wiring and boot-diagnostics.
Specs are named without tests/e2e/ and .spec.mjs. Paths are globs: * stays inside one folder, ** crosses folders.
The rules were built from what the specs touch: modules they import with page.evaluate, element ids and classes the module renders, and the API routes they hit or stub.

rules.why: REAPER export (#1071): the .rpp the zip endpoint adds (?reaper=1), the two export rows and their desktop-only branch, and the External editors setting
The note under the loudness cards after an older song was measured again (#923), and the seed that keeps the fixture songs from showing it.

The string tables. Specs that switch language or check translated text, the Guide sentences, and the queue strings (#799). A changed English string a spec asserts elsewhere surfaces at the pull request to main.
Which audio formats the backend's ffmpeg can encode and whether it can transpose, read through /api/health by the export menu's OGG button (#824) and its transposed-mix gate (#858)
The main stylesheet. Specs that measure layout (boundingBox, getComputedStyle, scroll and client sizes).
The import queue view, its library rows, and the stage text a running import shows
The mode switch and the mode menu, the stem picker and the lane stems popover

Lead + Backing: whether this install can make it (/api/health vocal_split), and what a split that did not work says and offers (#832). The e2e fixture never runs a real split, so the worker files only reach these specs through the state they report.
The import form: URL box, search, file drop, playlist import, and the stem choice submitted with it
Online search and link import are opt-in (#1089): the page's copy of the setting, the search box and composer that follow it, the Experimental settings tab, and the phone page's link field
Crash reports are opt-in and desktop only: the page's forwarding guard, and the Privacy settings tab with its switch and Last report view
Versions of a song (#804): the rows under a song in the library, the versions part of the Stems popover, the version-scoped mix and stem records, and the endpoints behind them
The library sidebar: rows, folders, tags, favorites, trash
A song or folder dragged while the library list rebuilds (#979): render() holds the rebuild until the drag ends

Settings > Separation: the per-stem model rows and their pure view (labels, Recommended tag, estimate, what a choice posts), the registry and settings behind /api/settings stem_models, and the moved device, quality and idle rows

The left column's width (--daw-col-w, 334 px in Advanced mode for the lane header's Model chip column): the stems panel, the label cell over the lanes and the master drawer's settings column are sized from it, and the waveform column takes what is left

The lanes' Model tab and its row (Advanced mode): the chip in its own column of each lane header between the key and the rail, the re-extract row laid out after the EQ and effects rows, and its pure rules (what the select lists, what a run's line says)

Settings > Separation > My models: the section and its pure view (the link rule, what is still missing, each row's status and reason), the (yours) and Add a model... options of the stem selects, and the /api/my-models routes, store, fetch and check behind them
catalog.js builds the Settings dialog: the Separation pane, its search entries, and the settings-applied and settings-answer events the Separation tab repaints from
Settings > Separation > Speed test: its pure view (table rows, estimated and measured labels, reason, what Apply posts), the /api/speed-test routes, the recommendation and the one-shot worker
Settings: navigation, every settings pane, and the config endpoint behind them
The artist and work dialog, and the lookups behind it
Discogs: the artist source and its token setting
Lyrics: the panel, the lane, sync and alignment, and the lookups
Song sections: lock, loop, rename, zoom, and the ruler
Tags: the bar under Sections, seeking, the digit keys, and their saving
Markers: the digit keys and their guard (main.js), the seek and the bar's scroll (transport.js), and the list read when a song opens (catalog.js)
Beat grid, metronome and count-in
Speed, pitch and transpose: the stretch stages and the pitch bus
The one speed and its box (setSpeed, stepSpeed, getSpeed, wireSpeedBox): the footer's fader and box, and Performance Mode's steps and box
Footer and transport layout
Recording: capture, takes, take folders, track inputs, meters
Lane headers are built by the take lanes and the record UI, so every lane spec reads them
EQ: the engine, the panels and the suggestions
Effects chains (Advanced mode): the engine, the pedals, the FX row and the export prints
Live input effects: an armed track's input heard through its chain while monitoring
Master bus, mastering and export
Stem storage format (#783): the MP3 storage stage and the engine an MP3 song opens on
Karaoke mode
Performance (streamer) mode

Sound and picture sync of a take with a camera: the export step's state in words and its nudge (syncControl.js, video/avSync.js), the sync route and the one picture placement on the server, and the loaded take it updates (takeLanes.js updateTakeEntry)
A lane's level as a number (the Studio fader's dB text, Performance's lane volumes and Monitor level)
Video: camera takes, the video lane and encoder settings
The Guide (help mode) overlay
The Donate button and dialog, and the two links it reads
We Recommend (#1092): the featured artist card above the partner grid, which artist is current and who is left out of the grid, its strings, its Guide entries and its layout
Notifications, failure reports and release cards
A failed import's cause sentence, its Try again, and the Resync result line (#175)
Format icon and cover art
Where playback resumes after a reload
The boot failure screen
The reason a failed request shows in the error box
The phone page and the QR code that opens it
